newsitem.title: USA: U.S. gives $14.5 million to save farms.
newsitem.headline: U.S. gives $14.5 million to save farms.

text.p: Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman announced Friday that the Agriculture Department will give $14.5 million to 18 states to help protect vulnerable farmland from urban sprawl.

The money from the agency's new Farmland Protection Program will be leveraged with state and local funds so that approximately $55 million will be provided to buy development rights from farmers to keep productive farmland in use.

"We don't think we can sit back and take our farmland for granted," Glickman told reporters. "As our cities sprawl into neighboring rural areas, our farms are in danger of becoming subdivisions or shopping malls."
The government intiative -- the first ever of its kind -- will protect at least 50,000 acres of productive farmland on 103 farms in 18 states, Glickman said.
The Farmland Protection Program was established in the 1996 Farm Bill with total funding of $35 million over six years.

Under the program, the Agriculture Department works with state and local projects to help acquire conservation easements or other interests in valuable agricultural land to limit nonagricultural uses of that land.

To participate in the program, states, tribes or local governments must submit proposals to the federal government to help provide matching funds to protect the land. The department received requests to protect 176,000 acres of framland in the first go-around. The agency then selected 50,000 acres of the best land in the most danger.

Proposals were selected from: California, Colorado, Connecticut, Delaware, Florida, Kentucky, Maryland, Massachusetts, Michigan, New Jersey, New York, North Carolina, Pennsylvania, Rhode Island, Virginia, Vermont, Washington and Wisconsin.
"We believe population growth will be exceedingly strong in the next decade ... We're trying to get ready to feed a hungry world," said Agriculture Secretary Glickman.
